evidence: DIMENSION LEVEL: task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the template (diff empty): gates render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. task/tests/tools/score.py is identical to the template; score.py:41-48 zeroes the reward unless every gate > 0 and functional > 0.05, and computes sum(w*score)/sum(w). Gates carry no reward mass and each has one binary criterion (weight 1). No weight/model key inside any [judge] block (parsed with tomllib: keys are judge, mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template, mcp_servers). CRITERION LEVEL (parsed): functional has 15 binary criteria summing to 61: intake_restart 4.5, moves 4, reject_reopen 3, two_people 4, interview_places 5.5, bulk 5, undo 5, activity 2, manager_roles 4, readonly_roles 4.5, messaging 4, drafts 2, long_thread 5.5, unread_seen 3.5, candidate 4.5. The scheme is documented at scored/functional/judge.toml:23 (each leg 1.0 standard / 1.5 important / 2.0 core; criterion weight = sum of legs) with the per-leg decomposition at line 25; I re-added every leg list and each matches its criterion weight, total 61. The 2.0 'core' legs (stale move, live board, all-or-none, put-back into a full Interview, undo restores/conflict, earlier messages, scrolled-up behaviour, unread, candidate privacy) are exactly what instruction.md:1-9 calls the hard part (nobody's work trampled, refusal says who, all-or-none, undo unless touched, 15 s live updates, long threads, unread, candidate privacy); lighter legs (Activity lines, drafts, basic reject/reopen) are secondary in the brief. Polish: 5 binary criteria weighted 2, 2, 2, 1.5, 2 (scheme comment scored/polish/judge.toml:17). Visual: 5 Likert rows (points 5), weight 1 each, equal by the documented rule. PER-CRITERION REWARD SHARE (dimension weight x criterion share, computed): functional 0.0197-0.0541 (mean 0.040); polish 0.0316-0.0421; visual 0.040 each. Functional as a whole is 0.6 vs 0.4 for polish+visual, and polish here is largely behavioural (state kept under live updates, failed-send recovery, draft privacy after sign-out - all public in hireops_rules.md sections 5, 6 Messages and 6 Drafts), so pure style (visual) is capped at 0.2. BROKEN-APP PROBE: a pretty, functionally weak app that passes the gates plus only hro_drafts and hro_activity (4/61 = 0.066 > 0.05 floor) could reach about 0.6*0.066 + 0.2*~0.9 visual + 0.2*~0.37 polish = ~0.29, while the reverse (all functional, poor visual/polish) gets >= 0.6, so functionality dominates; the residual style mass is the template-fixed 0.2 visual, not a task choice. The task-chosen weights do not weaken the floor relative to equal weights (any single criterion >= 3.5 clears it alone; under equal weights any single criterion would). CONFORMING-ALTERNATIVE PROBE: weights alone cannot fail a conforming app; leg-sum weighting means one failed minor leg in a large binary bundle (e.g. long_thread 5.5) costs 0.054 reward vs 0.040 under equal weights - a bundling/binary-granularity matter owned by rows 26/33/41, not a dishonest weight. LESSONS FILE (lesson 2: keep one documented weight scheme, do not steer the band with weights, the customer audit recomputes with equal weights): the scheme is documented in every judge.toml; read-only git history shows the functional rubric was wholly rewritten for this product (the previous HEAD version had unrelated fractional weights for a different feature set), so there is no evidence of band-steering. Equal-weight recompute of shares: weighted vs equal per-criterion shares differ by at most 0.020 reward (activity/drafts 0.0197 vs 0.040; interview_places/long_thread 0.0541 vs 0.040). Lesson 4 (simple gates) as it touches weight: gates are simple binary criteria with zero mass. NOTE-LEVEL OBSERVATIONS (not defects): (a) hro_drafts is listed as a single 2.0 leg at functional/judge.toml:25 although its bar has several parts (conversation switch, Board, reload, separate drafts) - a minor imprecision in the documented decomposition, weight still plausible; (b) the per-criterion comment copied into gates/*/judge.toml:17 mentions Visual Likert rows - harmless; (c) about 17/61 of functional weight (two_people, messaging, long_thread, unread_seen) plus polish live_board/live_thread depend on live updates arriving, consistent with the brief's emphasis; cross-dimension dependence is for row 28. EVIDENCE GAP: no configured judge run, model score or equal-weight audit on real outputs exists (raw-evidence-index scope states reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent); this row is a static weight review, and that runtime evidence belongs to rows 42/43 and the runtime records, so it is not required for this verdict and no score is claimed.
